problem: Existing robotics simulators typically offer either accurate contact physics (MuJoCo-based) or photorealistic rendering (Unreal/CARLA/AirSim), rarely both, and lack tools for controlled rare adverse visual conditions such as smoke, fire and rain. Related Unreal+MuJoCo work (SPEAR) is a Python Gym-style setup, not suited to full-stack ROS systems validation.
motivation: Vision-based navigation and SLAM need to be tested under adverse and out-of-distribution conditions that are hazardous or scarce in real datasets. A simulator combining deterministic, accurate physics with photorealistic dynamic effects enables repeatable benchmarking and synthetic data generation for sim-to-real research.
key_idea: Embed MuJoCo natively inside Unreal Engine (shared-memory, in-process, Unreal-first) so Lumen/Nanite/Niagara rendering and effects are combined with MuJoCo physics, with ROS/ZMQ middleware and a deterministic replay system.
insight: Benchmarks in the simulator show that ViNT/GNM and ORB-SLAM/MASt3R-SLAM degrade as smoke, rain and dynamic lighting increase (e.g., both planners get 0 success in Warehouse under major adversity), and a real tunnel smoke experiment shows the same trend. This suggests the simulated adversity reproduces real failure modes. Replay of identical trajectories under varied visuals isolates visual effects from motion. Sim-real feature alignment is only moderate (avg cosine 0.7094, KL 0.4739).
method: Unreal-first shared-memory architecture: MuJoCo runs in-process on a dedicated asynchronous thread inside UE, removing client-server latency and keeping determinism.

MuJoCo schema mirroring: MJCF is mapped to UE Actor/Component classes (AMjArticulation, UMjBody/Geom/Joint/Tendon, AMjManager); MJCF XML can be dragged in to auto-generate Blueprints, and UE levels can be exported back to MuJoCo.

Geometry conversion: AMjHeightfieldActor uses multi-threaded raycasts to make MuJoCo heightfields from UE landscapes/geometry; UMjQuickConvertComponent uses CoACD convex decomposition for arbitrary static meshes.
One-way mocap coupling: UE-driven actors (e.g., NavMesh NPCs) become MuJoCo mocap bodies; all MuJoCo sensors/functions are exposed to C++ and Blueprints, plus an MjSimulateWidget UI.
Middleware: modified ROS plugin or ZeroMQ bridge auto-maps sensors/actuators to topics, allowing controllers (Walk-These-Ways, VBC), planners (ViNT, GNM, NoMAD) and SLAM to run unmodified.
MetricManager and Replay System: log time-series to CSV and cache kinematics/sensor streams to replay identical trajectories across altered visual environments.
Adversity generation: Niagara smoke/rain/snow/pollution, dynamic lighting and NPCs at none/minor/major levels.

setting.backbone: Simulator/benchmark paper; evaluated pretrained GNM and ViNT (not fine-tuned), ORB-SLAM2/3 mono and MASt3R-SLAM, on a Unitree Go1 with Walk-These-Ways controller
setting.training_data: none (existing pretrained models evaluated without fine-tuning)
setting.observation: monocular RGB from Go1 onboard camera
setting.action_space: velocity commands to the Walk-These-Ways low-level legged controller (visual navigation with topological image graph)
setting.privileged: none (pre-built image topological map for goal navigation; GT poses only for SLAM evaluation)

numbers.eval_set_note: House env, no adversity, 5 runs per condition
numbers.extra: 5 runs averaged; simplified topological map; benchmark of others' methods in URL

numbers_note: Paper is a simulator paper; no navigation-benchmark SOTA claims. Only representative rows from its own benchmarks of existing methods are listed; full tables have 12 nav rows and 18 SLAM rows plus a real tunnel table (frames tracked: OrbSLAM2 7.83/0.00, OrbSLAM3 59.6/38.5, MASt3R 100/43.6 clean/smoky).
results: ViNT generally outperforms GNM in clean conditions (House none: ViNT SC 0.7333 vs GNM 0.3667), and both fail (SR 0) in major-adversity Warehouse. MASt3R-SLAM is the most robust SLAM (ATE 0.252-1.55 across conditions), while ORB-SLAM2/3 degrade. Sim-real image similarity is avg KL 0.4739 / cosine 0.7094.
limitations: No deformable terrain, only one-way kinematic coupling for UE-driven actors, and no validated depth/LiDAR noise models.
Sim-to-real gap only moderately quantified (cosine ~0.71) on hand-built scenes; small trial counts (5 runs) and adversity levels classified by human judgment; nav methods not fine-tuned.
